subject: Proposal: provisional invoice cadence + rolling credit threshold
messages:
From: Marta Klein <marta.klein@thermogen.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Oliver Rees <oliver.rees@thermogen.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract cadence question

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here has signaled OK on the commercials, but we need clarity on invoicing cadence and a short-term credit arrangement while our billing setup completes. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood invoice monthly (Net30) for the first 90 days, then move to quarterly invoicing once our AR system is fully integrated?
2) We request a provisional credit ceiling of EUR 120k during that onboarding window; ThermoGen will pay any accrued balance within 10 business days of each invoice. VAT: our tax team expects a reverse-charge approach (DE->US supplier) — they’ll share entity docs.

Attached is our PO and a quick procurement checklist. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks,
Marta Klein
VP Finance, ThermoGen
[Attachment: ThermoGen_PO_4591.pdf (14 KB, PDF)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Klein <marta.klein@thermogen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract cadence question

Hi Marta —

Appreciate the clarity and the PO. Quick response: we can support a provisional monthly invoice cadence for the first 90 days (Net30 terms) and then transition to quarterly billing. A couple of practical notes:

- For the provisional credit ceiling, Redwood can extend a temporary EUR 100k credit line while procurement completes entity verification — we typically require tax docs & a signed amendment for any credit > EUR 75k.
- Since ThermoGen is EU-based and requesting reverse-charge, our tax team will need the VAT registration and the EU entity details (to be reflected on the amendment).
- Payment timing: Net30 default; if you can commit to payment within 10 business days per invoice, we can add a 1% early payment allowance on the first two invoices as a small operational concession.

I’m looping in Ben from Finance and Marissa from Account Management to formalize the amendment and confirm the interim ceiling. If you’re available tomorrow at 10am CEST we can do a short call to finalize.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf (7 KB, PDF)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marta Klein <marta.klein@thermogen.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract cadence question

Marta / team —

Thanks for the note. From Finance perspective:

- We can provisionally approve EUR 100k credit for 60 days contingent on: (a) receipt of VAT registration + entity verification, (b) signed amendment accepting the provisional cadence.
- If ThermoGen needs EUR 120k ceiling as requested, we’ll require a security mechanism (either an escrow retainer for the EUR 20k delta or a corporate guarantee).
- Invoicing specifics: invoices generated on the 1st of each month for the previous month; Net30 due date. If payment arrives within 10 business days we can offer a 1% operational rebate on that invoice (applied as a credit on the next invoice).

I’ve attached a template amendment that includes the provisional credit line language and the VAT evidence checklist. If you can provide the entity doc (Tax_Entity_Verification.xlsx) we’ll expedite approval.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf (9 KB, PDF); Attachment: Tax_Entity_Verification.xlsx (12 KB, XLSX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Klein <marta.klein@thermogen.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract cadence question

Hi Marta —

Following up after Ben’s note. Quick summary of next steps so nothing gets lost:

1) ThermoGen to send VAT registration & completed Tax_Entity_Verification.xlsx (we need the VIES confirmation or equivalent).
2) Sign the Draft_Amendment_v2 (Ben has included the escrow option if you want the EUR 120k ceiling without corporate guarantee).
3) Confirm whether you’d like Redwood to invoice on the 1st (month-in-arrears) or to back-date to your requested monthly cadence (we recommend 1st of month for bookkeeping simplicity).

Happy to put a 20-min slot on the calendar for Thursday if you want to run through edits live.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Klein <marta.klein@thermogen.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Oliver Rees <oliver.rees@thermogen.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract cadence question

Marissa / team —

Thanks, all. We discussed internally and can confirm the following:

- We will provide the VAT registration and completed Tax_Entity_Verification.xlsx by EOD tomorrow.
- ThermoGen accepts the provisional EUR 100k credit line; to get to EUR 120k we will be able to provide a short-term escrow deposit of EUR 20k to bridge the delta — please send escrow wiring instructions.
- Invoice cadence: please invoice on the 1st of each month for the previous month (month-in-arrears). We will aim to remit within 10 business days per invoice.
- DocuSign: please send the updated amendment and we’ll prioritize signature.

Appreciate the flexibility — we’ll be on the call Thursday at 10am CEST to finalize language.

Best,
Marta Klein
VP Finance, ThermoGen
[Attachment: Signed_PO_4591.pdf (5 KB, PDF)]
